grammar.form: turn it off / look after him

explanation.en: With a separable phrasal verb a pronoun object must go in the middle: 'turn it off', never 'turn off it'. Inseparable ones keep the particle attached: 'look after him'.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbekchada bunday bo'linish yo'q, shuning uchun olmosh joyi tez-tez xato bo'ladi.

grammar.label: so / such / too / enough — full system
grammar.form: so + adj; such a + adj + noun; too + adj; adj + enough

explanation.en: 'Too' means more than you want; 'enough' means the right amount. 'So' and 'such' intensify and usually lead to a result clause.
explanation.uz: 'too' — keragidan ortiq; 'enough' — yetarli. 'so' va 'such' kuchaytiradi va odatda natija ergash gapiga olib keladi.

grammar.positive_example: It was so cold that we went home. The bag isn't big enough.
grammar.negative_example: It was such cold that we went home.

l1_notes.uz: 'enough' sifatdan KEYIN, otdan OLDIN keladi — bu tartib o'zbekchada boshqacha.

phonology.label: Assimilation of place — ten past, good boy, that cup

functions.label: Checking understanding and asking for clarification

exponents.text: Sorry, do you mean the first one or the second?
Could you explain what you mean by that?
Do you mean the blue one?
So you're saying it's closed on Monday?
Sorry, could you say that again?

functions.label: Describing a problem and complaining politely

exponents.text: Excuse me, there is a problem with my room.
I'm sorry, but the heating isn't working.
This is terrible! Change it now!

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: The heater will not turn off. I have tried everything.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Have you switched it off at the wall?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: I switched it off, but it came back on.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then pull the plug out. Do not just turn it off.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Sorry, do you mean the plug behind the sofa?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That one. The room is too hot to sleep in.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: It is. And the window does not open far enough.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Could you explain what you mean by that?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: About this much. There is a bolt that blocks it.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then take the bolt out. Do you have a spanner?

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Somewhere. It is such a small job, but it takes all evening.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: They always do. I will look for the spanner.
